identity.name: Allura Red AC
identity.chemical_class: Synthetic monoazo sulfonated food colorant (disodium salt)

function.mechanism: Provides red color via an azo-conjugated chromophore that absorbs visible light; sulfonate groups increase water solubility.
common_food_categories: foods generally (unless a standard of identity prohibits added color)

adi.basis: EFSA re-evaluation retained ADI at 7 mg/kg bw/day; 2013 statement found no reason to revise; 2015 refined exposure remained below ADI in assessed groups.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA kept ADI at 7 mg/kg bw/day; refined exposure assessment indicated exposures below ADI across assessed populations.

adi.basis: WHO/JECFA database lists ADI as 0-7 mg/kg bw and latest evaluation year 2016.

concerns.summary: Mouse studies reported worsened experimental colitis susceptibility and microbiome perturbations after chronic Allura Red/Red 40 exposure.
A 2023 mouse/in vitro study reported DNA damage signals with Red 40 under experimental conditions.
A 2024 review summarized potential neurotoxicity mechanisms for synthetic food dyes including Allura Red AC, with limited direct human causal evidence.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2013 statement did not revise the ADI of 7 mg/kg bw/day.
EFSA 2015 refined exposure estimates were below ADI in assessed population groups.
A 2025 in vitro study found no significant short-term cytotoxicity or major microbiota-composition changes under tested conditions.

populations: children (1-10 years) in conservative 2009 EFSA high-exposure scenarios
adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA 2009 estimated potential exceedance in some child scenarios; EFSA 2015 refined assessment indicated exposures below ADI for assessed groups.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory approvals and ADIs remain in place, but credible animal/mechanistic signals (colitis susceptibility, inflammation, DNA damage signals) and historical child-focused exceedance scenarios support a cautionary middle-tier classification rather than risk_free or high.
key_factors: EFSA ADI retained at 7 mg/kg bw/day with 2015 refined exposures below ADI
FDA approval under 21 CFR 74.340 with certification/GMP conditions and no GRAS pathway for color additives
JECFA ADI 0-7 mg/kg bw (latest evaluation year listed: 2016)
Recent animal/mechanistic studies indicating gut and inflammatory concerns
